research_focus.current_question: Across previously untested numerical candidate pairs, do L1H0 and L4H0 exhibit context-stable causal pair/token directions that generalize more reliably than arithmetic correctness?

active.title: L3H3 four-versus-five specialized causal bias
active.statement: In mature MathGPT v0.3, L3H3 exhibits a comparatively four-versus-five-specific causal candidate-selection effect that does not generalize as broadly across adjacent numerical candidate pairs.

confidence.label: unscored
confidence.note: Registered from an evidence-grounded L11A synthesis proposal. No calibrated confidence score has been assigned.

open_questions: Does the L3H3 four/five effect replicate across new prompt families while four and five are held fixed?
Does L3H3 respond similarly to other semantically or lexically related token pairs?
Is the apparent specialization caused by token identity, pair contrast, or prompt context?

supporting_findings.title: L3H3 four-versus-five-specific fixed-pair signal
supporting_findings.statement: EXP-0006 identified L3H3 as a four-versus-five-specific fixed-pair causal signal rather than a broadly generalizing arithmetic-correctness head.

supported.title: Four-versus-five causal token preference
supported.statement: In mature MathGPT v0.3, L1H0 may causally bias the four-versus-five decision toward 'four', while L4H0 may bias the same decision toward 'five', across multiple numerical contexts.

confidence.label: replicated_causal_support
confidence.note: The hypothesis has support-only evidence from at least two distinct completed experiments, including replicated E3 causal support.

open_questions: Does L1H0 continue to favor four when prompt semantics change while four/five candidates remain fixed?
Does L4H0 continue to favor five under the same controlled changes?
Is the effect lexical, numerical-semantic, or task-dependent?

supporting_findings.title: Four/five direction is consistent for L1H0 and L4H0
supporting_findings.statement: Across the four EXP-0004 contexts that directly contrasted four and five (A03, A04, A05, C03), the causal signs were consistent with intact L1H0 favoring four over five and intact L4H0 favoring five over four in all four contexts.

supporting_findings.title: EXP-0005 preregistered four-versus-five causal replication
supporting_findings.statement: Across 12 preregistered fixed four-versus-five contexts, intact L1H0 causally favored four in all 12 probes while intact L4H0 causally favored five in all 12 probes, including both four-correct and five-correct contexts. L4H1 also passed the preregistered weak-control criterion.

tested_by.title: Fixed four-vs-five causal context transfer
tested_by.question: When the candidate tokens four and five are held fixed while prompt semantics change, do L1H0 and L4H0 retain opposing causal directions?

supported.title: Cross-pair numerical candidate-selection bias
supported.statement: In mature MathGPT v0.3, L1H0 and L4H0 participate in candidate-token or candidate-pair selection mechanisms whose causal directions generalize across multiple numerical candidate pairs more reliably than they track arithmetic correctness.

confidence.label: unscored
confidence.note: Registered from an evidence-grounded L11A synthesis proposal. No calibrated confidence score has been assigned.

open_questions: Does each head preserve a consistent lower/upper or token-identity direction across number pairs outside P23/P34/P45/P56?
Are the effects tied to lexical number tokens, numerical magnitude, candidate ordering, or pair identity?
Do the same candidate-selection biases appear in non-arithmetic contexts using the same number tokens?

supporting_findings.title: Broader fixed-pair token-bias signals in L1H0 and L4H0
supporting_findings.statement: EXP-0006 found broader fixed candidate-pair causal direction signals for L1H0 and L4H0 across multiple non-control number pairs, indicating that their effects are better described by candidate-token or pair identity than by a stable arithmetic-correctness role.

supporting_findings.title: EXP-0007 independent cross-pair candidate-selection replication
supporting_findings.statement: In mature MathGPT v0.3, EXP-0007 independently replicated cross-pair causal candidate-selection behavior for L1H0 and L4H0 on four previously untested numerical candidate pairs. Both heads passed within-pair directional stability on 4/4 new pairs, while strong arithmetic-correctness tracking did not pass (L1H0 10/16; L4H0 8/16). The P45 positive control and L4H1 weak-control criterion both passed, and both primary heads showed pair-dependent rather than uniform lower/upper orientation.

requirements_for_future_reasoning: Distinguish verified raw evidence from curated scientific findings.
Do not treat planned experiments as evidence.
Trace scientific claims through findings to source experiments and verified artifact identities.
Preserve finding, experiment, evidence, and hypothesis checkpoint identities during scientific review.
Do not invent confidence scores when the confidence engine has not evaluated a hypothesis.
Preserve evidence level when comparing findings.
